newsitem.title: FRANCE: French voters gloomy, whoever wins election -poll.
newsitem.headline: French voters gloomy, whoever wins election -poll.

text.p: French voters are gloomy about the prospects for the economy, taxation and the labour climate, whether the left or right wins a parliamentary election at the end of the month, a poll released on Thursday shows.

As far as taxes are concerned, 33 percent expect no change if the current centre-right government returns to power, but 44 percent see tax going up, while 39 percent see stable tax if the Socialists win and 42 percent expect a rise, the poll says.
The poll by the BVA institute for the monthly Enjeux-Les Echos magazine and Publicis Consultants was carried out on May 9-10 with a sample of 922 people of voting age.
Thirty-six percent of those sampled expect no change in the economic situation if the Socialists come to power, 36 percent see it getting worse and 19 percent see it getting better.
If the centre-right wins, 42 percent see no change, 35 see the economic situation getting worse and 16 percent expect an improvement.

In France, where the labour climate is often volatile, the poll shows a greater degree of confidence in the Socialists' ability to improve things. While 36 percent see no change in the labour climate, and 28 percent expect it to get worse, the score for the right is 44 percent see things deteriorating and 40 percent see things remaining as they are.
